audit_result.proof_trace: The invariant (exactly one role per generation) relies solely on application-level checks in createGenerationRole, but updateGenerationRoles performs a bulk delete-then-insert using a caller-supplied array that is only filtered for generation >= 0 and non-empty discord_role_id — no deduplication by generation key. Combined with the absence of a DB UNIQUE constraint on generation_roles.generation (confirmed by Phase 02c note), an admin can insert duplicate generation entries. Downstream callers of .single() on the duplicated generation will fail, breaking role resolution for affected members.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An admin calls updateGenerationRoles with a roles array containing two entries with the same generation value; both pass the validRoles filter and are inserted, leaving the DB in a state where subsequent .single() lookups for that generation throw errors, blocking Discord role assignment for all members in that generation.

PROP-docker-compo-inv-006.text: Each generation must have exactly one role mapping in generation_roles table.
PROP-docker-compo-inv-006.assertion: forall g in generations: COUNT(generation_roles WHERE generation == g) == 1
